user.title: Connect to LibreNMS
user.description: Enter the URL of your LibreNMS instance and an API token. Create the token in LibreNMS under Settings → API → API Access, for a dedicated user with the Global Read role. A Normal User only sees devices explicitly assigned to it, which is usually none.

data_description.url: The base address of your LibreNMS instance. Subpaths are supported, and the API path is added for you. If you leave out the scheme, https is used.
data_description.api_token: The token value shown in LibreNMS API Access.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only if your instance uses a self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate LibreNMS
reauth_confirm.description: The API token for {url} was rejected. Enter a new token.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure LibreNMS
reconfigure.description: Change the address of your LibreNMS instance, its API token or its certificate setting. All devices, entities and their history are kept.

data_description.url: The base address of your LibreNMS instance. Subpaths are supported, and the API path is added for you. If you leave out the scheme, https is used.
data_description.api_token: Leave empty to keep the current token. Enter a new one when moving to a different LibreNMS instance.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only if your instance uses a self-signed certificate.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect. Check the URL, that the instance is reachable from Home Assistant, and the SSL setting.
error.cannot_connect_https_assumed: Could not connect to {url}. No scheme was entered, so https was used. If your instance only serves plain http, enter {http_url} instead, knowing that the API token will then cross your network unencrypted. If it uses a self-signed certificate, turn off certificate verification instead.
error.insufficient_permissions: LibreNMS accepted the API token, but its user is not allowed to list devices. Give that user the Global Read role.
error.invalid_auth: LibreNMS rejected the API token. Check that it still exists under Settings → API → API Access.
error.invalid_url: That does not look like a valid URL.
error.redirected: LibreNMS answered with a redirect to {redirect_url} instead of the API. If that is the address of your LibreNMS instance, enter it as the URL. The API token is never sent to a redirected address.
error.redirected_reauth: LibreNMS answered with a redirect to {redirect_url} instead of the API, so a new token will not help. If your LibreNMS instance has moved, close this dialog and use Reconfigure on the LibreNMS integration to change its URL, and its token if needed. The API token is never sent to a redirected address.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: This LibreNMS instance is already configured.

data_description.scan_interval: How often to poll LibreNMS, in seconds. Lower values detect outages faster but put more load on the instance.
data_description.include_disabled: When enabled, devices marked disabled or ignored in LibreNMS are included in the device totals and the up/down counts.

insufficient_permissions.title: LibreNMS API token lacks permission
insufficient_permissions.description: LibreNMS at {url} accepted the API token but refused to return devices or alerts (HTTP 403). The user the token belongs to needs the Global Read role. Change it in LibreNMS under Settings → Manage → Users. The integration recovers on its own at the next update; there is no need to enter a new token.
